signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Holds ~$57 through the FOMC round-trip; caught between a hawkish Fed and the sticky-inflation/war premium
signals.detail: Silver spot ~$57 (Thu 30 Jul); gold ~$4,080 near a record; copper ~$6.44/lb
signals.takeaway: The book's single most important line item held its ground through the FOMC selloff-and-rebound: silver stayed around $57 while equities round-tripped, supported by the sticky 3.3% core PCE, the reignited US-Iran conflict (oil >$92) and haven demand offsetting the higher 10Y. Silver is in a two-sided pull — a hawkish Fed and 10Y ~4.68% are the bearish real-rate channel, while the inflation/war premium is the bullish one. Structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 avg). Hold the core and hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into a live September hike risk.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: US-Iran pause stays BROKEN: Brent holds >$92 (WTI ~$84) on renewed US strikes and Hormuz attacks
signals.detail: Brent >$92, WTI ~$84 (Thu 30 Jul) after the +7-8% spike (Brent $90.74/WTI $84.46 Wed); 60-day ceasefire in shambles, strikes resuming both sides
signals.takeaway: The dominant cross-portfolio driver stays flipped: the US-Iran fighting pause remained collapsed through Thursday — a fresh wave of US strikes and Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping kept Brent above ~$92 after Wednesday's ~8% spike, with the 60-day ceasefire effectively in shambles. Double-edged for the book: it re-arms the inflation/rate-hike fear pressuring the rate-sensitive core (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) as the Fed stays hawkish, but restores the geopolitical bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Trade the escalation-vs-de-escalation odds; the Red Sea/Hormuz front is the live risk, but don't chase the spike given OPEC+ spare capacity.

signals.name: US Treasuries / rates
signals.label: Sticky core PCE (+3.3%) validates the hawkish Fed; 10Y ~4.68%, 2Y at fresh 2026 highs; September a live hike risk
signals.detail: Fed held 3.50-3.75% (9-3, three hike dissents); June core PCE +3.3% y/y, Q2 GDP +1.5%; 10Y ~4.68% (+~10bp), 2Y >4.2% (2026 high), DXY ~100.8
signals.takeaway: Thursday's data validated the hawkish hold: June core PCE stayed sticky at +3.3% y/y (headline +3.7%) even as Q2 GDP slowed to +1.5% — a stagflation-lite mix that vindicated the three FOMC hike dissents and pushed the 10Y up ~10bp to ~4.68% with the 2Y at fresh 2026 highs. That is the direct higher-for-longer headwind for the book's highest-beta pain (levered silver, gold miners) and S-REITs, and September stays a live hike risk. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder. Duration got no bid even on the growth slowdown — favor the belly/quality IG over the long end until the data genuinely softens.

signals.name: Gold / gold miners
signals.label: Pushes to ~$4,080 near a record on the sticky-inflation/haven bid; largest weekly fund inflow since April
signals.detail: Gold ~$4,080 near a record (Thu 30 Jul, +0.4%); gold funds +$2.0bn (wk to 22 Jul, largest since April); DXY eased ~100.8
signals.takeaway: Gold pushed to ~$4,080 near a record on Thursday — gaining even as equities rallied — as sticky 3.3% core PCE, the oil spike and the reignited Iran conflict drew a haven and inflation-hedge bid that outweighed the higher 10Y and a softer dollar. It held far better than the beta names and drew the largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April (+$2.0bn), with multi-month central-bank buying a structural floor. Favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage as the steadier metals hold and the cleaner hedge against the Iran pause staying broken; BofA's flagged elevated net-longs are the near-term warning.

signals.name: Semiconductors / AI-capex
signals.label: Semis REBOUND as AWS +37% and MSFT's record gain re-validate AI-capex; Burry adds to his Micron short
signals.detail: SMH bounced Thu 30 Jul with the Nasdaq +2.8% (best day of year); AMZN AWS +37% to $42.2bn, capex raised ~$220bn, AMZN +9% AH; MSFT record 1-day value gain; Burry added MU short 24 Jul at $933.86
signals.takeaway: The AI-chip narrative reversed hard: after >$1trn was wiped since 24 Jul, Amazon's AWS +37% blowout and raised ~$220bn capex plan — plus Microsoft's record one-day market-value gain — re-validated the AI-infrastructure spend, and semis rebounded with the Nasdaq's +2.8% best day of the year. A relief for the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core. But Michael Burry disclosed adding to his Micron short (24 Jul at $933.86) inside an expanded NVDA/MU/AMAT/SOXX bear book arguing the group sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band — the standing warning that the rebound runs into rich multiples. Favor the internet/platform names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core; treat the chip leg as higher-beta and two-sided.

signals.name: Rare earths (ex-China basket)
signals.label: Lynas makes first ex-China terbium; MP/USAR on China entity list; 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
signals.detail: Lynas first commercial-scale terbium oxide outside China + reported ~US$96M DoD deal; MP & USAR on China dual-use entity list (22 Jun); broad MOFCOM controls SUSPENDED to 10 Nov 2026
signals.takeaway: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist: Lynas produced the first commercial-scale terbium separation outside China (a heavy-REE milestone) and advanced its ~US$96M US DoD supply deal, while MP carries DoD backing (~15% stake, $110/kg NdPr floor) and Energy Fuels builds out White Mesa. But MP and USA Rare Earth sit on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun) and the broad October-2025 MOFCOM controls are suspended only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3.5 months out) — the calendar catalyst. This stays a strategic optionality play on the controls snapping back, not an immediate momentum trade: accumulate MP and government-backed UUUU on weakness into that 10 Nov cliff.

signals.name: Tencent / HK tech
signals.label: Tencent suspends buyback into a 12 Aug-results blackout; internet sleeve still favored over the SMIC chip leg
signals.detail: Tencent buybacks (1.1M sh/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) SUSPENDED from ~22 Jul into a 30-day blackout ahead of 12 Aug results; record China inflow (+$21.3bn) the prior week; Xiaomi buyback 3.9M sh/HK$100.7M (15 Jul)
signals.takeaway: The HK-tech core's internet names had been decoupling from the global chip rout and drew a record China weekly inflow (+$21.3bn) under the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal — but Tencent has now suspended its near-daily buyback from ~22 Jul, entering the customary blackout ahead of its 12 Aug interim results, temporarily removing a mechanical corporate bid into a jittery, post-FOMC tape. Xiaomi's own buyback continues. Favor Tencent/Xiaomi (internet/consumer) over the SMIC chip leg while the AI-capex unwind runs, but don't add aggressively before the 12 Aug print; US risk-off and a hawkish Fed are the near-term beta headwinds, and the pre-selloff China inflow needs the 31 Jul Flow Show to confirm it held.

congress.deepDive: A fresh exit from the semis leader during the AI-capex-peak scare that has since partly reversed. Sits opposite the Micron/AI bulls (Newhouse) and alongside Burry's standing chip shorts — the congressional book splitting on the AI-capex debate. A direct read-through to the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core, which the AWS/MSFT rebound has relieved near-term.

The META/MSFT legs land right into their post-close prints (MSFT +3% AH, META -7% AH). Lands the same day as Liccardo's NVDA sell, capturing the two-sided AI-capex debate within Congress.

A diversified rebalance rather than a single directional call.

A rare direct overlap with the portfolio's PM-miner sleeve, and well-timed as oil re-spiked ~8% on the Iran-pause breakdown.

The Intel leg lands as INTC restructures under state/government-backstop chatter; the Uber leg extends the household's mega-cap tech/mobility tilt. No new Pelosi PTR has surfaced since — this remains the freshest trackable trade.

congress.deepDive: A rare GSE/housing-finance play among congressional books, tied to the on-again talk of releasing Fannie/Freddie from conservatorship. High-idiosyncratic-risk single name, minimal overlap with the portfolio.

superInvestors.name: Scion / Michael Burry (personal)
superInvestors.rationale: Having deregistered Scion with the SEC in late 2025 (now publishing 'Cassandra Unchained' on Substack, 300K+ subs), Burry trades personally and discloses only via the newsletter — his last 13F (Q3 2025) held NVDA/PLTR puts (~80% of the book), and he has since expanded chip shorts (NVDA, MU, AMAT, SOXX, TSLA, CAT), disclosing on 24 Jul that he shorted MORE Micron at $933.86 — arguing the SOX sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band and AI-capex can't justify valuations.
superInvestors.deepDive: The cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis — but it is now under pressure: after the semis complex shed >$1trn from 24 Jul, Thursday's Amazon AWS +37% blowout and raised ~$220bn capex, plus Microsoft's record one-day gain, re-validated AI spend and rebounded the chips (Nasdaq +2.8%). His fresh 24 Jul MU short (at $933.86) sits directly opposite Tepper's big Micron weight and the crowded AI-infra longs (Ackman MSFT, Bridgewater, Tiger) — the marquee two-sided AI debate. No 13F any longer — the newsletter is the only window; self-reported, sizes approximate, not SEC filings.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.value: AAPL+GOOGL now ~30% of the equity book
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire's Q1 13F nearly tripled its Alphabet stake to ~57.8M shares (~$16.6B) while cutting Chevron ~35%, cutting Constellation Brands ~95%, and fully EXITING Visa, Mastercard, UnitedHealth and Amazon — a decisive quality-AI tilt under Greg Abel alongside a continued record cash build (~$397B at Q1-end).

A striking contrast with Duquesne's Q1 GOOGL exit. Q2 13F due 14 Aug — confirm the sell-streak and any new adds then.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Bill Ackman's Q1 13F (filed 15 May, ~$13.7B, top-3 Brookfield/Amazon/Uber ~51%) added a new Microsoft stake, built by end-May to ~$2.4B (funded by trimming Alphabet), and lifted Amazon to ~$2.4B (now 2nd-largest). He has said he initiated FOUR new positions to be revealed in the Q2 report, and continues building Howard Hughes (~46.9%) as a 'modern Berkshire'.
superInvestors.deepDive: The new MSFT stake (~5.65M sh, instantly his #4 at ~15% of the book) looks well-timed after Microsoft's record one-day market-value gain on 30 Jul; Amazon remains a crowded whale consensus (also top for Tepper) and jumped ~9% AH on the AWS +37% beat. The four teased positions plus the Pershing Square USA IPO prep make his 14 Aug 13F one of the most-watched of the cycle. He slashed Alphabet ~95% in Q1 — the opposite of Berkshire's aggressive GOOGL add.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper's Q1 book (filed 15 May, ~$5.93B / 31 positions) is led by Amazon (~15%), Micron (~9.5%), Alphabet, Uber and TSM; he added heavily to memory (Micron) and kept 'buy China' (Alibaba top, KWEB add). No July 13D/13G surfaced — carried pending the 14 Aug Q2 13F.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper's Amazon conviction makes it the single most-consensus mega-cap long across the tracked whales (also top for Ackman) — vindicated by AMZN's ~9% AH pop on the AWS +37% blowout (30 Jul). His big Micron weight sits directly opposite Burry's fresh 24 Jul MU short; the pair is the sharpest memory-cycle bull/bear split as chips rebounded on the AI-capex re-validation. His only new Q1 position (SanDisk) was also initiated by Druckenmiller — a quiet two-whale memory bet.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne Family Office
superInvestors.rationale: Stanley Druckenmiller exited Alphabet entirely and opened a new Broadcom stake while adding SanDisk, Seagate and Micron across many new positions in Q1; top holding Natera (~18%). Nothing new verified mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: High-turnover repositioning that leans into AI-storage/semis (AVGO/SNDK/STX/MU) while dropping GOOGL — a sharp contrast with Berkshire's ~$16.6B Alphabet build and a stance now tested hard by the July AI-capex/memory rout.

superInvestors.rationale: Chase Coleman added TSM (+49%), Applied Materials (+85%), Broadcom (+25%), Meta (+12%) and Nvidia in Q1, plus a new ~$72M Intel stake; top holdings GOOGL (~$4.2B), NVDA (~$2.8B), AMZN (~$2.6B). No verifiable mid-cycle move this run.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tiger leaned hard into the AI-semis supply chain in Q1 — a stance now under pressure from the >$1trn semis drawdown and Burry's chip shorts. Carried pending the 14 Aug 13F.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: George Soros's fund held an S&P 500 put as its top position ($773M) and added NVDA, TSM and EA while cutting Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft in Q1 — a hedged, cautious posture. No new 13D/13G surfaced mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: The large index-put top holding is a portfolio hedge that looks prescient into the 28-29 Jul FOMC selloff — capturing the defensive tilt among some whales into a stretched tape. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust held a concentrated ~$31.7B book (top: Berkshire, Waste Management, Canadian National, Caterpillar, Deere) with no notable individual change and no July 13D/13G filing — a low-turnover, blue-chip reference book.
superInvestors.deepDive: Included as a stable long-horizon 'permanent capital' benchmark; its concentration and inactivity contrast with the high-turnover hedge funds. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Trump / Trump Media (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Forbes pegs Trump's net worth at ~$6.1B, dominated by the ~41% DJT stake and ~$1.4B of crypto-linked lines. A 19 Jul SEC corporate update detailed Trump Media's crypto-treasury build — ~9,542 BTC (~$593M) plus a ~$2B additional BTC purchase (~$2.6B total) — while recent DJT Form 4s are RSU grants, NOT open-market buys.
superInvestors.deepDive: The crypto exposure and DJT concentration dominate the net-worth picture, tying DJT's book to crypto beta — which held up better than equities this week (BTC ~$64k, resilient through the FOMC selloff). The absence of any insider open-market purchase and the RSU-heavy Form 4 activity are the recent corporate developments.

superInvestors.name: Bridgewater Associates

superInvestors.deepDive: Included for roster completeness; no material change verified this run (gap).

Xiaomi remains a high-beta HK-tech name that swings with the HSTECH tape and offers relative catch-up if the rally broadens on Politburo follow-through.
